newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Telecom Co puts value at $4-6 bln. [corrected 15:00 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Telecom Co puts value at $4-6 bln. [corrected 15:00 gmt]

text.p: (Corrects to make clear that Bulgaria Telecom Co hopes for a bid valuing the company between $4-6 billion, not that company hopes for a $4-6 billion bid.)
Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC) said on Wednesday it had stabilised its finances for a planned partial privatisation and hoped for a bid valuing the company at $4 to $6 billion.
BTC Director Marian Dragostinov, who was appointed in February, told a news conference the government would determine the size of the stake to be sold.
He said the best buyer for BTC would be a consortium of leading operators which would invest in developing the company.
He said BTC could raise the price by participating with Mobikom, which has a joint venture with Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc, and another foreign operator in buying loss-making operator Mobiltel.
Mobiltel has a GSM, or Global System for Mobile telecommuncations, licence to operate a digital phone system. Mobikom operates an analogue system.
Mobikom, set up in 1992, is building up Bulgaria's major mobile cellular telephone system.

"We will try to combine with Cable & Wireless the advantages of the analogue mobile system with the advantages of the GSM system...and then, investment for covering the country would be reduced about three times," Dragostinov said.
Mobiltel, a joint venture set up by Bulgarian private financial group Tron, was granted the GSM licence two years ago.

Dragostinov said BTC's new management had inherited financial chaos but had imposed strict discipline through cutting expenditure and staff, and introducing new sources of funds and a reasonable tariffs policy.
"From the beginning of the year until the end of May, BTC paid the state some $19 million (in taxes) and by the end of the year, the company will pay a total of $108 million," he said.
"The stable financial state of the company is essential for the privatisation process, which is expected to last a year."

Dragostinov said that during the first four months of 1997 the company had generated income of 84 billion levs ($49 million) from its core activities alone, while its expenditure was 48 billion levs. Total BTC income last year was 36 billion levs.
Average monthly income now is some 35 billion levs and BTC plans to increase it to 50 billion levs per month through the development of new markets.
Dragostinov said BTC had begun to profit from international telecommunications traffic by renting out networks.

"In 1996, some 10 percent of the income was due to rented channels and the remaining percentage was coming from conventional clients. Our goal this year is to increase it to 40 percent," Dragostinov said.

He said BTC welcomed the introduction of a currency board set for July 1. Stricter financial discipline would be favourable for the company, which is owed millions of levs by the state television and radio.
